source.title_on_document: Sketching vs. AI Prompt Based Design Intent Evolution in Undergraduate Students: an Exploratory Study

supplement.where: The paper refers to no supplementary material, online appendix, or data repository.

paper_design_summary: Sixty-one 8th-semester industrial design students in four student groups did a one-hour individual design task (ideas to promote conscious water use at home). The four groups were randomly assigned to two conditions: sketching with pen and paper (groups A+C, n=31) or free use of AI tools of their choice, LLMs and text-to-image models (groups B+D, n=30). Three design professors rated the creativity of image-level ideas with the Consensual Assessment Technique, and the authors counted ideas, idea categories, and recurring concepts.

studies.label: Design task: sketching vs. AI (water-saving concepts)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Four intact student groups were randomly assigned to two conditions: sketching only (groups A and C) or free use of generative AI tools (groups B and D). Two groups per arm; the paper does not say how groups were formed or how the randomization was done.
assignment.quote: In a second phase, the design task was carried out with four student groups, randomly assigned to two predefined conditions: sketch groups A+C (n=31) and AI groups B+D (n=30).
assignment.locator: p. 4, Section 3.2.2; Figure 1 (p. 3) labels A and C 'control (sketch)' and B and D 'experimental'

arms.name: Sketch groups A+C
arms.description: Pen and paper only; no devices allowed. Photographed sketches with annotations.

arms.name: AI groups B+D
arms.description: Own laptops or smartphones; free choice of currently available AI tools (LLMs such as ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Copilot; text-to-image tools such as Krea.AI, Leonardo.AI). No prior prompting training.

participants.exclusions: No participants are reported as dropped from the creativity, fluency, or category analyses (rated ideas come from n=31 sketch and n=30 AI students, p. 4). Only image-level ideas with an explanatory description were rated; AI images that were too abstract and that students discarded were excluded, and AI image variations of one idea counted as one concept. For the prompt thematic analysis (not an outcome here), 3 of 30 AI logs were discarded as incomplete, leaving 27 (p. 10). The diagnostic questionnaire was optional and answered by 42 participants (p. 5).
participants.who: Industrial design bachelor students in their 8th semester (4th of 5 years); 38 female, 23 male; ages 21 to 30 (mean 22); recruited through design teachers as a creative workshop within their regular mandatory course.
participants.country: Not stated explicitly for participants. Both authors are at UNAM, Mexico City, and the paper describes sketch solutions around the 'tinaco', a 'characteristic element of Mexico City dwellings' (p. 6).
participants.quote: The study involved 61 industrial design bachelor students in their 8th semester, which is the 4th year of a total of 5 years of design studies.
participants.locator: p. 3, Section 3.1; arm counts p. 4, Sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.3

ai_tool.name_model: Participants' own choice. LLMs: ChatGPT GPT-4o free (n=23), GPT-4o Plus (n=2), DeepSeek-R1 (n=3), Copilot (Azure-hosted GPT-4-class) (n=3), Gemini 2.5 (n=1). Text-to-image: Leonardo.AI (Phoenix) (n=15), Krea.AI (Krea 1) (n=8), Meshy.AI (n=2), Vizcom (n=2), PromeAI (n=1), ArtGuru (n=1), GenCraft (n=1). Study carried out in April 2025.
ai_tool.how_used: Free use of chatbots to generate and develop ideas, plus text-to-image tools for images; 28 of 30 students generated images in text-to-image tools from prompts written by the LLM (p. 9). Image generation was also an AI role.

task.description: Individual open-ended product design brief: 'how can we promote conscious water use in the home by its inhabitants?' Generate various ideas and detail a few; document process (sketch photos or AI conversation logs and images). Creativity was rated on image-level ideas (sketch or AI image plus explanatory text).
task.duration: About 1.5 hours: 30 minutes for explanation and documentation, 1 hour for the creative exercise (p. 4).

outcomes.name: Expert-rated creativity of image-level ideas (Consensual Assessment Technique, 1-5)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Three design professors (10+ years experience) rated each image-level idea (image plus explanatory text) on a five-point scale (1=not creative, 5=highly creative), two rounds with the second in reverse order; ICC (two-way random, consistency) = 0.67 (95% CI 0.55, 0.76). 115 ideas rated: 71 sketch, 44 AI. Table 1 also gives medians and the share of ideas in four score ranges.

contrasts.reported: Mean score per idea: Groups A+C (sketch) n=71 2.52 vs Groups B+D (AI) n=44 2.89; median 2.67 vs 3.00; low range (1-1.9) 18.3% vs 9.1%; medium (2.0-2.99) 52.1% vs 29.5%; medium-high (3-3.99) 26.8% vs 54.5%; high (4-5) 2.8% vs 6.8%. n are ideas. No SD and no test for the pooled comparison; the paper calls the result 'not conclusive'.

Group A (Sketch, n = 54, M = 2.36, SD = 0.61) vs. Group C (AI, n = 24, M = 2.94, SD = 0.58); t(76) = -3.995, p < .001; d = 0.60, 95% CI [-0.98, -0.47]. n are ideas. The printed CI does not contain d and its target is not stated.
Group B (Sketch, n = 17, M = 3.04, SD = 0.62) and Group D (AI, n = 20, M = 2.82, SD = 0.68); t(34.8) = 1.039, p = .306. n are ideas.

outcomes.name: Fluency: total ideas per participant (text and image ideas)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of all ideas at the total idea level: written ideas and sketches (sketch arm) vs LLM-generated text ideas and text-to-image images (AI arm). Total 89 ideas in sketch groups vs 291 in AI groups.

contrasts.reported: A total of 89 total ideas were generated by the sketch groups and 291 ideas for the AI groups; the mean for AI is 9.7 ideas per participant and 2.8 for sketching. No SD or test.

outcomes.name: Fluency: image-level ideas per participant
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of image-level ideas (sketches or AI images with explanatory description) included in the rating document: 71 from 31 sketch students, 44 from 30 AI students.

contrasts.reported: 31 students generated 71 ideas based on sketches, and 30 students generated 44 ideas with AI on an image level; average of 2.2 ideas per participant with sketches vs 1.4 ideas with images in the AI group. No SD or test.

outcomes.name: Flexibility: idea categories explored per student
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each participant's total ideas sorted by hand into 12 author-defined categories (A. raising awareness by measuring water use ... L. gamification/educational challenges); average number of categories per student.

contrasts.reported: AI groups (B+D) present more categories than sketch groups (A+C), with an average of 4,2 versus 2 categories explored per student. No SD or test.

outcomes.name: Category coverage of each condition's pooled ideas (total idea level)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of ideas per category for each condition's pooled total ideas, shown as bubble charts. Read from Figure 5: sketch groups have ideas in 9 categories (A 16, B 26, C 2, D 29, E 6, F 5, G 3, H and I 1 each; sum 89) and none in J, K, L; AI groups have ideas in all 12 (A 83, B 39, C 2, D 59, E 9, F 4, G 3, H 5, I 4, J 30, K 22, L 31; sum 291). The bubble-to-letter matching for H and I in the sketch chart is read from the figure.

contrasts.reported: Figure 5: 'The AI chart shows a greater number of explored categories'; categories J, K, L 'emerged in the AI group but were not explored by the sketch group.' Counts per category are printed in the bubbles only; no test.

diversity_detail.metric: Number of the 12 idea categories with at least one idea in the condition's pooled set, and ideas per category.
diversity_detail.computed_over: All total-level ideas of all participants in a condition, pooled and hand-coded into categories.
diversity_detail.notes: This is breadth of the pooled idea set, not pairwise similarity. AI arm also has far more ideas (291 vs 89), so coverage is not adjusted for pool size.

outcomes.name: Homogenization of image-level concepts (share of AI students with the same concept)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Authors' qualitative reading of final image-level outcomes. In AI groups, 18 of 30 students (60%) produced a shower or faucet with a color-changing light ring indicating water use. For sketch groups the paper says images 'displayed more diversity' but gives no comparable count.

contrasts.reported: AI arm only: 'a common idea among AI groups, with 18 out of 30 students (60%) coming up with this concept.' Sketch arm: 'the images displayed more diversity depending on the type of solutions focused on local context' (no number). No test.
contrasts.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2.2; p. 7, Figure 4 and Section 4.2.3

diversity_detail.metric: Share of participants in a condition whose image-level idea matches one recurring concept (light-ring shower/faucet).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Image-level ideas of AI-arm participants, inspected by the authors; no matching measure for the sketch arm.
diversity_detail.notes: Sign: lower diversity in the AI arm (homogenization) as the authors describe it; the comparison with the sketch arm is qualitative.

eligibility.reason: Four student groups were randomly assigned to sketching vs free AI use (p. 4, Section 3.2.2), so people received AI through a cluster-level random assignment with only two groups per arm; the paper does not describe the randomization procedure and calls itself an exploratory study. 61 students analyzed (31 sketch, 30 AI), above 50. Creativity of each idea was rated by three expert professors (CAT), and ideas and categories were counted on the output. Weak points for the reviewer: two clusters per arm, all statistics at the idea level, and group labels in the t-tests that conflict with the design description.

one_line_finding: With 61 design students in four randomly assigned groups, AI-group image ideas averaged 2.89 vs 2.52 for sketch ideas on a 1-5 expert creativity scale, significant in one group pair (t(76) = -3.995, p < .001) but not the other (t(34.8) = 1.039, p = .306), while AI users produced more total ideas (9.7 vs 2.8 per participant) and categories (4.2 vs 2 per student) but fewer image ideas (1.4 vs 2.2) and converged on one concept (18 of 30) (pp. 6-7, Table 1, Sections 4.2.1-4.2.3).
open_questions: Group labels conflict: the design section and Figure 1 put sketch in groups A and C and AI in B and D, but the t-tests in Section 4.2.1 label Group A and Group B as 'Sketch' and Group C and Group D as 'AI' (A n=54 + B n=17 = 71 sketch ideas; C n=24 + D n=20 = 44 AI ideas). Which groups were compared in each test is unclear.
Assignment was of four intact groups, two per arm. Should a cluster-randomized design with two clusters per arm meet criterion 1?
Design class: the task was a supervised workshop session inside a mandatory course; lab_rct chosen, field_rct is arguable.
The printed 95% CI [-0.98, -0.47] for d = 0.60 does not contain d; it may be an interval for the mean difference.
notes: All creativity statistics are at the idea level (n = ideas), not per participant; no participant-level SDs or pooled test of A+C vs B+D are reported. The AUT (Top2 scoring by three experts, Cronbach's alpha 0.65) was a pre-task diagnostic, not an outcome of AI use; the paper reports within-arm Pearson correlations of AUT with task fluency (sketch r=.12, p=.54; AI r=.08, p=.67) and task creativity (sketch r=.12, p=.53; AI r=-.30, p=.103) (p. 7, Section 4.2.4), which are not treatment contrasts and are not listed as outcomes. The AUT range groups (25 + 36 + 7 = 68) do not sum to 61 (p. 5). Exit-survey perceptions, design-path coding (Figure 6), and prompt-style thematic analysis (Table 2) are qualitative or self-report and are not listed. Search record evidence ('N=61') matches the paper.
